question: On which date did ISRO attempt its 101st launch, which could not be accomplished due to technical problems during its third stage?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun May 18 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ISRO's 101st launch attempt** was scheduled on **Sun May 18 2025**, marking an important milestone in India's space exploration journey.
 
• During this attempt, ISRO faced **technical difficulties** in the rocket’s **third stage**, leading to the launch failure.
 
• The third stage is crucial for placing the satellite into its intended orbit, and any malfunction can compromise the mission's success.
 
• ISRO has had an impressive record of successful launches, and such failures often lead to comprehensive analysis and improvements for future missions.
 
• Despite this setback, ISRO’s achievements in space technology continue to position India as a prominent player in the global space community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation):**

 
 
• Founded in **1969**, ISRO is India’s national space agency under the Department of Space.
 
• It is headquartered in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka.
 
• ISRO has been instrumental in launching satellites for **communication, navigation, remote sensing, and exploration**.
 
• Prominent missions include **Chandrayaan** (lunar exploration), **Mangalyaan** (Mars Orbiter Mission), and the **Gaganyaan** (human spaceflight mission).
 
 
 
• **Stages of a Rocket:**
 
 
• Rockets are typically composed of multiple stages, each powered by its own engine and fuel system.
 
• The **first stage** provides initial thrust to lift the rocket off the ground.
 
• The **second stage** further propels the rocket after the first stage is discarded.
 
• The **third stage** ensures the satellite reaches its orbit, which is critical for mission success.
 
• Failure in any stage can result in mission failure, emphasizing the need for rigorous testing and quality control.
 
 
 
• **ISRO’s Achievements:**
 
 
• ISRO has successfully launched over **100 missions**, including satellites for India and international clients.
 
• It developed the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)**, which is considered one of the most reliable launch vehicles globally.
 
• ISRO’s **Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)** made India the first Asian nation to reach Mars orbit and the first globally to do so in its first attempt.
 
• India’s **Chandrayaan-3 mission** successfully landed near the Moon’s South Pole in **2023**, showcasing ISRO’s growing capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Space Exploration:**
 
 
• Space missions are vital for technological advancements, scientific discovery, and economic growth.
 
• They provide critical data for **weather forecasting, disaster management, and communication**.
 
• ISRO’s missions have also contributed to **international collaborations** and strengthened India’s global presence in space science.
